name: KY-024 linear hall magnetic sensor
identification: Long narrow black PCB with a blue box-shaped trim potentiometer with a brass screw, an 8-pin chip and 4 angled header pins, and a tiny flat black three-legged chip at the far end. The KY-036 has a bent metal pin on a similar black part there.

confirmations.question: Read the 4 pin labels printed on the linear hall magnetic sensor. Are they AO, G, + and DO?
confirmations.reason: Clone modules differ. The wiring plan is only valid for a module with exactly these labels.

facts.statement: The module has four pins: analog signal (AO), ground (G), supply (+) and digital signal (DO). Go by the printed labels.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-024, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi, Pico or micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published. The technical data names 5 V as the functional range, depending on the components, so whether it measures well from 3.3 V is not confirmed.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-024, wiring tables and technical data

facts.statement: A comparator drives DO high when the magnetic field exceeds the threshold set with the trim potentiometer, and a second LED on the module lights. AO carries the direct measurement, inverted: a higher measured value gives a lower voltage. Powered from 3.3 V, neither output can rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-024, 'Functionality of the sensor'
